title: cdr_bang_bang_jtol Step 1: Alexander early/late mapping appears reversed, and there is no timing diagram for the three samples
evidence: docs/06_design_insights/cdr_bang_bang_jtol.md:35-36: 'if E_k = D_{k-1} != D_k the edge sample looks like the previous bit -> clock LATE; if E_k = D_k != D_{k-1} -> clock EARLY', with the convention (line 38) 'delta t positive when clock early'. Physical check from first principles: the edge sampler fires at the nominal data-transition instant; if the sampling clock is early it fires BEFORE the transition and still sees the old bit D_{k-1}, so E=D_{k-1} should mean clock early (delta t > 0), and E=D_k means late. As printed the two cases are swapped relative to the page's own sign convention, and the sign(delta t) loop in the mermaid then has the wrong feedback polarity if a reader follows it literally. This is the first place an EE who has never seen an Alexander PD gets lost: three sampling instants (D_{k-1}, E_k, D_k) are described only in words, with no picture. (Confidence: derived by me from the sampling geometry, not from the Alexander paper; please verify against Alexander 1975 / Razavi before editing.)
proposal: Add a small figure cdr_alexander_timing.png: a 4-row timing diagram with x = time over 2 UI, rows = data eye with a transition at t=0, sampling clock (data samples at +/-UI/2, edge sample at 0), and three clock placements (early, aligned, late) with the sampled bits E, D_{k-1}, D_k annotated and the resulting early/late/none truth table.
